exposure: Emergency uterine artery embolisation (e-UAE) for intractable haemorrhage associated with laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy (LAM)
outcome: Overall obstetric complication rate (preterm birth, abnormal placentation, postpartum haemorrhage)
cohort: The study participants were 38 women who underwent emergency uterine-artery embolisation (e-UAE) for uncontrollable bleeding during or within 24 hours of laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy (LAM).
finding: Emergency uterine artery embolisation (e-UAE) effectively controls catastrophic bleeding after laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy (LAM) without compromising future fertility, with observed live-birth rates and the spectrum of obstetric complications similar to those reported after uncomplicated myomectomy.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery occurred in 62.5% of births following e-UAE.
